Hi, I would like to work on this if the following design direction matches what you have in mind.

I propose adding a persisted session visibility value (normal / hidden), defaulting to normal, and exposing it on session creation. Session list APIs would exclude hidden sessions by default and support an includeHidden query option that is preserved in pagination cursors.

Direct lookup by ID would remain unchanged. Parent/child traversal and deletion would explicitly include hidden sessions, while ordinary TUI and app discovery would filter hidden sessions from both list responses and live session events.

I would add focused coverage for persistence/migration, list filtering and pagination, direct lookup, parentage independence, deletion, and user-facing discovery.

Would this design be acceptable, and may I take the issue?

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #38849: Same SQLITE_BUSY root cause from concurrent OpenCode processes with `busy_timeout=0` — in that case triggered by multiple VS Code windows
- #33320: Same `database is locked` / SQLITE_BUSY error when launching concurrent headless `opencode run` workers

The underlying problem appears to be the same: the shared SQLite database has `busy_timeout=0`, so any concurrent write from two processes (or two subagents) fails immediately instead of retrying.

Also hitting this on **1.18.10**, but in the **browser web UI against a headless server** — no Electron involved. That may help narrow the cause, since this issue and #39840 are both Desktop/renderer reports.

## Environment
- opencode 1.18.10 (`opencode-ai` from npm, `latest` tag), Linux x64
- Run as a systemd **user** service: `opencode serve`, bound `0.0.0.0:4096`
- Accessed over the network in a normal browser (not the desktop app)
- Served bundle: `assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js`

## Error
Full-page "Something went wrong / An error occurred while loading the application":

```
Error: Stale read from <Show>.
    at h2 (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:10382)
    at C1 (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:10580)
    at TD (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:7024)
    at Cg (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:6602)
    at tw (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:8043)
    at AV (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:8926)
    at lse (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:8298)
    at Jo (http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:8228)
    at http://localhost:4096/assets/index-BBRqEIzV.js:2:6717
```

Same shape as the Desktop reports (`castError` → `handleError` → `runComputation` → `updateComputation` → `runTop` → `runQueue`), just minified differently.

## Notes
- **Not Electron-specific.** Reproduces in a plain browser, so the renderer/packaging layer can be ruled out.
- **Server side is clean.** Nothing in `journalctl` or `~/.local/share/opencode/log/` at the time of the crash — the failure is entirely client-side.
- Restarting the service and hard-reloading the browser does not help; the same bundle hash is served before and after.
- Possibly closer to #28928 (stale `<Show>` after a `/global/event` network error) than to the Desktop folder-switching reports, given this is a remote server over the network where the event stream can drop. I did see an unrelated upstream socket drop in my logs during the same period, though I have **not** confirmed any connection.
- The UI reports its version as **1.18.9** while the binary is 1.18.10 — that appears to be #36232. Mentioning it only so the version string isn't confusing if it shows up in screenshots.

## Trigger
I don't yet have a reliable reproduction — I hit this during normal use and haven't isolated the exact action, so I can't say whether it's fresh page load, session switching, or an event-stream drop. I'll follow up with the browser devtools console (including anything preceding the error) once I catch it again with devtools open.
